spine: C first (Modern C), then the machine under it (CS:APP), then modern C++ (C++ Primer -> Effective Modern C++ -> the library -> concurrency). Placement pretest skips what's known.
rules: Every lesson has a 'predict / fix / write' practice: predict the output (or 'undefined behavior'), fix a bug, write one small function.
All code is compiled with warnings and sanitizers on (-Wall -Wextra -g -fsanitize=address,undefined); a Compiler Explorer link is fine when not at a machine.
Code from grade-B books is never copied into a lesson (library/README.md): cite the section or exercise number and write fresh code.

courses.title: Placement
courses.note: One pretest across CP101-CP204: per course, predict (output or UB?), fix (find the bug), write (a short function, graded free response). Sets which courses are done by exam and which sections each remaining course teaches.
